title: Europe: only Dixieland group, Hitler and jazz, playing in a palace
summary: All the other American groups were modern; an Austrian said Hitler banned jazz. The Straws played a palace benefit with Lorenz Graham and others.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, who, who did you hear over there? Did you listen to any bands on your way back?

Uh, well, we just, uh, had the opportunity to catch, uh, De Parry's band in New York, but over there, I mean, uh, uh, all the groups that were sent over there were all modern jazz groups. We were the only, uh, Dixieland group, you know, on this tour, see. Everything else was, uh, modern jazz. Most of the, uh, people from over there, the Austrians themselves, they, they have bands in the different nightclubs and all, and they all play modern jazz. So, uh, to hear Dixieland was something different for them, you know. I had one fella tell me that during the war that, uh, Hitler outlawed, uh, jazz. He would not let the people listen to jazz because there was only one thing, you know, that they should adore, and at the time it was him. And anybody caught listening to jazz records or anything that they, you know, took a particular interest in, they were jailed, you see. So now these people are loose and free, they can, you know, they can listen to and say what they want, see. Uh, I tell you, they, they really, really liked listening to the music. Every place we played, a place was just packed, you know. So, oh, golly, we had, we had a chance of playing, uh, castles. We played in palaces. I, I guess those little walls never figured they'd ever be listening to Dixieland jazz, huh?
Where was this, at Vienna, that area you played in, castles? Yeah, mm-hmm.

Yeah, we went to this, uh, all this great palace, I forget the name of it. But, uh, they had, uh, some kind of benefit on for the, uh, Austrian free youth. And they used our group, they asked us to play. And they also asked us, there was a Negro boy, a fella by the name of Lorenz Graham. He accompanies himself with a guitar, he sings folk music, you know. And, uh, they had, uh, the Stan K. Quintet, that was a modern group. And, uh, we had about, I guess about five, five different groups that put the show on, see. And, uh, we played in a castle, huh, or a palace. And, that's, uh, that's something out of the ordinary. I mean, you just don't play in palaces every day, you know.
